purpose: W2-C: allocate the existing Auction-bound canonical Inventory reservation when the existing canonical Deal is created from an awarded Auction basis; no parallel Deal, Auction or stock engine.
authorization: Owner instruction on 2026-09-05 to continue PC-CROP with existing push/PR/merge authorization. Implementation remains blocked until this finite scope is independently accepted and registered in immutable base-state authority.

excludedAfterSourceAudit.reason: The generic industrial CI already discovers the existing Deal suite; W2-C must not widen or weaken the global workflow to admit one bounded slice.
The checker discovers additive migrations dynamically; changing the checker would weaken independence of the migration gate.
The existing DR driver is generic; W2-C restore assertions belong in the already-run restored database acceptance and Auction acceptance evidence.
The synthetic canonical Deal is intentionally not an Auction-origin Deal. W2-C must not modify that fixture to manufacture an allocation bypass.
The closed canonical lifecycle test consumes the existing synthetic Deal and need not change for an Auction-origin creation invariant.
W2-B registration/reservation authority remains unchanged; W2-C end-to-end allocation is exercised at Auction execution and Deal authority boundaries instead.
W2-C does not change RESERVE/RELEASE quantities at DRAFT; it adds an immutable allocation sub-claim while the existing lot reservation remains RESERVED.
No application Auction command contract is changed; the existing close/bind authority is reused and its integration is proven by the live Auction atomic suite.

requiredInvariants: Reuse the existing Auction award, DEAL_BASIS_READY event, PrismaDealRepository, canonical Deal, Inventory position/reservation and existing audit/outbox authorities; do not create DealV2, InventoryV2 or a parallel market engine.

A Deal created from an inventory-bound Auction lot must commit one immutable normalized stock allocation linked to the exact Auction inventory binding, award, winning bid and canonical Deal before the create receipt can commit.

Winning quantity is derived server-side from the authoritative winning bid using the binding's pinned profile/unit rules. Browser quantity, source, verified or ownership claims never become authority.

Partial winning quantity allocates only that exact quantity and records the exact still-reserved remainder. The original lot reservation remains RESERVED until a separately accepted lifecycle transition; DRAFT allocation itself is not commitment, shipment, acceptance, sale or independent verification.

Current seller and buyer users, memberships, organizations and tenant scope are revalidated before mutation and before every replay response. Revocation cannot replay a previously valid create receipt as current authority.
Deal, participants, stock allocation, Auction award binding, Deal event, audit and outbox commit atomically at READ COMMITTED under a stable lock order and payload-bound idempotency.
A replay may verify existing allocation evidence but must never repair a missing allocation after a create receipt already exists.

Application Deal INSERT cannot bypass inventory allocation by omitting Auction inventory evidence, by SET ROLE, caller-controlled fixture flags or a legacy SECURITY DEFINER owner. Historical non-Auction controlled fixtures remain explicitly outside this Auction-origin invariant.
The canonical 18-key Deal sagaState remains backward-compatible; normalized inventory links are stored separately rather than changing the signed/hashed commercial basis shape.
The inventory reservation release/reuse guard remains effective after canonical RLS policy overlay, one-deal reset and database restore; no broad DML grant is introduced.
Registration, Role Eligibility, Federal Accounting lock #4321, packages, lockfiles, external provider claims and production topology remain unchanged.
acceptance: Restricted PostgreSQL and HTTP/service tests prove exact full and partial winning-quantity allocation, replay, changed-payload conflict, stale/missing binding denial, cross-tenant and same-tenant outsider denial.
Revoking either current seller or current buyer membership/user/organization authority makes a subsequent create replay fail closed rather than return the historical receipt.
Missing allocation evidence, audit, outbox, actor authority or award linkage rolls the complete Deal creation back; no partially acknowledged Deal or stock mutation remains.
A bound reservation cannot be released, rewritten or reused while its awarded lot/Deal allocation exists; remainder arithmetic and stock conservation are exact integer atoms.
Existing Auction race/winner tests and canonical Deal tests remain effective; legacy non-Auction controlled fixtures are not silently converted into authoritative stock evidence.
The generic forward-only migration checker, global CI workflow and generic DR driver pass unchanged, proving W2-C did not modify its own independent gates.
Forward migration chain, no public schema drift, one-deal, restore, cryptographic freshness and exact-head CI/review pass.
remainingTerminalBoundary: Committed/shipped/accepted/sold lifecycle, genealogy, custody/title/restrictions and immutable TradeRiskAcknowledgement remain later W2 slices.
RFQ/Offer/Negotiation inventory consumption remains separately accepted; this slice covers the existing Auction-to-Deal path only.
User-facing stock-to-lot-to-Deal UX, warnings/acknowledgement and verified REG.RU runtime acceptance remain required before terminal INVENTORY/DOUBLE_SELL_PROTECTION/UNVERIFIED_TRADING credit.
